name: Live updates
tagline: Webhooks to a change feed, polled every 15 s
summary: Open pages update on their own when something changes on GitHub. A pull request merged elsewhere shows up within about 15 seconds, with no reload.

flow.label: GitHub webhook
flow.note: The GitHub App delivers an event such as pull_request, push or check_run.

flow.label: Webhook route
flow.note: Checks the HMAC signature, answers 202 and records changes in the background.

flow.label: Event to entity keys
flow.note: Maps the event to keys such as pull:owner/repo#12 or checks:owner/repo@sha.

flow.label: github_change table
flow.note: Upserts one row per entity with a rising version; rows are swept after 15 minutes.

flow.label: Changes endpoint
flow.note: Returns keys newer than the cursor, filtered to repos the user can read.

flow.label: Change feed poller
flow.note: Polls every 15 s while the tab is visible and invalidates only matching queries.

features.name: Webhook intake
features.summary: Verifies the signature, caps the body at 25 MB and replies 202 before writing. Installation events instead drop the cached installation token.

features.name: Entity keys
features.summary: Twelve kinds of key say what changed: pull, issue, repo, checks, run, release, labels, milestones, collaborators, discussions, settings, org.

features.name: Cursor and expiry
features.summary: The cursor is a version plus issue time. If it is over 14 minutes old or 2,000 rows behind, the client refetches every on-screen query once.

entry.role: Reads rows after a cursor from D1

features.name: Private repo filter
features.summary: Public repo changes go to anyone. Private ones only reach users who can read the repo through the GitHub App; the list is cached 60 s in memory, 10 min in KV.

entry.role: Repos the user can read, with caches

features.name: Entity to query registry
features.summary: One table maps each query group to the entity kinds that affect it. Cross-repo lists and the inbox refetch only if the changed item is already in them.

entry.role: Does this cached query care about this change

features.name: Own-write invalidation
features.summary: When you comment, merge or edit in DiffKit, the same entity keys are applied right away, so your own change does not wait for the webhook.

features.name: Polling, not sockets
features.summary: One small request per tab every 15 s, plus on focus and reconnect. An earlier WebSocket relay on a Durable Object was removed in commit 5886c02.

entry.role: Hook mounted once in the signed-in layout
Poll loop, cursor and visibility rules

goodParts: handleGitHubWebhook and handleChangesRequest take their dependencies as arguments, so each has a test file that runs without a Worker.
github.query.test.ts fails when a query key group is neither mapped to an entity kind nor marked exempt in the registry.
watch: docs/github-cache-architecture.md (437 lines) describes the removed design; its banner says it stays until a replacement is written, and data-fetching.md now exists.
Repos without the GitHub App send no webhooks, so they refresh only on focus or stale time (docs/data-fetching.md, L2).
The private-repo list stops at 10 pages of 100 repos per installation (github-change-access.server.ts:19); larger installs fall back to refetch on focus.
